The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has crossed 10,000 confirmed cases, with nearly 4,900 deaths. About 80 percent of new infections are being detected outside known networks of contacts, making it harder for health authorities to trace and contain the virus.
The outbreak is being driven by the Bundibugyo virus, for which there is no specifically approved vaccine. Conflict, displacement, gaps in diagnostic testing and limited access to healthcare are further complicating the response.
